When something is undiscovered, does that mean it doesn't exist? Or when it is discovered, does it magically come into being? Or vice versa so that it comes into being the second before it's discovered?
And if you don't believe in something, does that thing not exist for you? Say, for instance, you and a friend were in a haunted house. You don't believe in ghosts, but your friend does. Can you not see it because you do not believe in it, or can you friend see it because his mind is more open and the presence registers more in his mind.

If I'm sitting in this chair, I have sufficient evidence that it does exist and that I can't wish it away or not believe in it to make it leave this reality. But, the opposite of the last point is true. You can make something come into reality by believing it. Most people would call this either :excersizing one's will" or "having faith."

author: Chaos Creator
content:
He looked around slowly. Such a dirty little shithole he lived in. The walls and ceiling were cracked and ragged with huge, gaping holes revealing the skeletal inside frame of the filthy hovel. If he had been in a better state of mind, perhaps he'd have seen the irony of the resemblance of this place to his life. Holes ripped to exposed the ugliness beneath. But metaphors weren't exactly his forte...
He lay on a urine stained, rock hard cotton mattress upon the floor. The only object in the room other than the toilet, the sink, and a gaunt and frail looking little table that never held food. A dusty and very dim bulb lit the pathetic scene from above, causing shadows to leap in and out of the holes in the walls.
He couldn't exactly remember when it had become like this. Nothing really seemed clear any more. Like the the apartment, his mind was covered in a veil of dust and haze. The only thing that pervaded in his mind between senseless, pointless thoughts, was the thought of the one he had once loved.
She had been his world. His life. He ate, slept, and believed her. She was what held him bound to the earth. They had been together for 3 years. Had even been married for 6 months when everything came crashing to a sudden end.
Before the incident happened, the two had been so happy together. They went everywhere together. It was almost as though they were the same person. And being like any normal young people, they liked to hang out with friends and party.
He liked to smoke pot and drop a hit or two of acid every now and then. She liked to get all spun out on meth or coke. And so the parties went for a long time.
Until one night someone offered the beautiful young lady a shot of heroin. Her lover wasn't around to say no, so she jumped at the opportunity. She and the one that had offered it went to a back room and rigged up.
A few hours went by, and the young man began to get anxious at the nonattendance of his wife. He began to move about and look for her, finally pushing his way into the small back room.
There he found his lovely bride lying in a pool of her own vomit, clothes ripped off, her eyes rolled far back in her head. Screaming for help, he cradled his love in his arms. She seemed lifeless... and indeed she was.
The police came and took the body away after concluding that she had rigged way too much and passed out, at which point the person that had given the drug to her, raped her unconcious body.
The poor young man was crushed. His mentality went to almost nothing. He would simply sit and stare off into space for endless periods of time. He could no longer hold a job. He could barely care for himself. He had become an empty husk.
Forced to live on a disability check sent from the government, he isolated himself in a tiny apartment in the worst area of the city they had once lived so happily.
And now he simply waited to die...

"Def Comedy Jam. That'd be a pretty funny video to get," I thought.
I looked up at the t.v. Jerry Springer was back on, now. Fucked up and slightly retarded, but funny, nonetheless.

But at that moment, I was relaxing, stoned chillin', reflecting on the days events. Thinkiong about the new friend I had made. And the family member I might soon lose.
But first you have to know the whole beginning of this little story. Like I sad, it's been a stressful couple o f weeks.
Well, for starters, I lost my job. I had been working at an industrial manufacturing plant. Apparently, I pissed main boss off somehow. Talking too much shit, I guess. But, hey, he was a fucking dick. A truly crooked dick (hehe... that was wath is called a double entendre. just thought I'd thow that fact in there). He'd never pay on time, and, then, when he did pay, it was short. But it was a job.
Anyway, he fired me. So I was out of a job. Which meant I didn't have any money. Which meant I couldn't buy my girlfriend's gas and cigarettes. Which, apparantly, pissed her off.
And, so, she broke up with me. It was only a day later I found out she had cheated on me. That was pretty pleasant.
So, then, since I wasn't spending all my time with my girlfriend, I got bored. I watched t.v., but not really. I'd play guitar, but not for very long. I didn't really feel like it.
So, I got on the internet, and went to the site where I posted all of my stories and poems. I went to the forums and started replying to the questions, conversations, and debates there. Human Contact was my self-prescribed medication. I began to interact. And I found a friend.
JadeFlame25's fianceé, who was pregnant with their child, didn't want anything more to do with him. And, then, he found out she cheated on him. So, we were pretty much in the same boat, I guess.
We started talking everyday over instant messages and through the forums. we even started our own li'l brand of role playing on the forums, "Hotel California".
And role playing was what we were doing on the day I started on the downward spiral (thank you disappointedinwonderland).
My grandmother took my great-grandmother, who is 87, to the doctor. Only to find out that something was seriously wrong. They had to send them to the biggest hospital in the area.
My grandpa told me after he got off the phone with my grandma that he was going with them. Which lef me in the house, alone, with no cigarettes, and an empty feeling of worry.
So, I began to write. Three poems and two songs on guitar in less than an hour. But, then, I was restless again. I had nothing else to do, but get on-line. Luckily, JadeFlame was on. I told him what was going on and that my nerves where shot. He told me just to be calm and not do anything stupid.
"I don't know if I can take someone else close to me dying. I can only take so much shit before I break. And I feel like it's getting close," I told him.
He said, "What happens when you do?"
"My room gets destroyed, random things are broken, mysterious cuts show up all over me. And I hit, yell or ignore everyone else. Usually. But I don't know about this time. I'm much more stressed than all the other times," I replied.
"But that's life, my friend," he told me. "Plenty of your relatives, friends and loved ones are going to die in your life. It's sad, but it's a fact of life."
"But I'm so tired of it all already," I returned.
"You have people that care about you, I'm sure. Friends?"
"I don't have any friends," I said. "They've all left me, stabbed me in the back, or died."
"Then don't kill yourself for me. Someone you've never met face-to-face. Someone you've only known a few days. I know we don't really know each other, but I consider you a close friend."
And immediately I was at a loss. A complete stranger that actually gave a shit? I thought that was a dead thing...
I thanked him, and told him that I appreciated his words, but told them that I had to go see what was going on.
I knew nothing of the situation, but I called my mom and old her what was going on. She started to call around, and had me call around to all the hospitals they could possibly be at.
No one knew anything. None of them could find my grandparents. So, my mom told me to come over to her house and crash for the night.
So, after an hour of silent, reflective driving, I sat down and smoked a bowl with my mother. We calmed each other with our mutual presences. My mom's boyfriend and his son were there, and they helped diffuse the tension somewhat. We called around some more. Nothing. It had been two hours, and still no one knew a thing.
Which leaves me where I am now, lying in bed, wondering... waiting. If someone else close to me dies, I'm not sure I can handle it.
Will the downward spiral continue? Or will everything be alright, or at least not as bad?
All I can do is wait...

author: Chaos Creator
content:
I turn my face to the western sky. The sun's setting finally. The colors of the sunet are my blood. I see in shades of gray. As the last bit of light slips over the burning fires of the horizon, I turn to continue my walk home.
The trees bend low to my royal procession. Wait. there's one that isn't kneeling. Bring me this ingrate. Dare to disobey me? Death to you. Waves of pulsing energy exit my fingers and strike the lone tree, sending a scatter of sparks into the growing night.
The procession continues. Down dirt and gravel roads paved with gold and precious jewels. A glint up in the heavens catches my eye. I hate to look up that way. Reminds me of times long ago. The glint grows to become a shimmering light. Have they come already?
The light begins to take shape, and then it lands. Standing before me is an angel. Clothing of pure white, wings of pearly feathers, emanating righteousness. And she's beautiful. Her face, her body, her air.
Why have you come? You know. No, I don't. Tell me. Your salvation is what brought me here. Salvation? I need not your false idols and images. But I am here, refuting that falseness, yet you turn away... Look that way. See the fires burning in the west? What color are they? The most wonderful shades of orange and pink that He can create.
She looked at me. And what do you see now? She looked back to the horizon and a look of astonishment and fear passed over her angelic features. Pain, death... How?
I have the power, my lovely... I move up to stand behind her, my lips near her ear. I do not need the jealousy of your god. I decide my own fate. I am my own god.
She whispers. How do you have such power to rival His reign? My hands rest upon her hips and my lips move a bit closer to her ear, and I, too, whisper.
It's inside. It's inside us all. Including you. Why do you remain cowed under your god's oppressive hand? Do you not see that to truly be powerful, you must free yourself?
Her eyes close and her hands begin to tremble. I can tell I'm getting through to her. She believes what I say. I have her broken. She turns her face toward mine, her features a mere inch from mine. Her eyes open, looking pleadingly into mine.
I smile. You want the power, don't you? Yes. Then join me... Our lips meet and we kiss passionately. The kiss of Fate. This angel once again belongs to me. My heavenly mate from above.
The darkness continues to deepen. And during our night of carnal lust and desire, she gives herself to me fully. And sees me for what I... we, truly are... Fallen Angels.

content:
A prequel to the one I wrote off the top of my head. (And by the way, I penned this one in the same manner... improvisationally)
The handle of the knife slipped from my grip as I tried to wrench it free from the hole I had just created. Not really surprising considering all the blood jetting everywhere. Her face was a mask of agony as I grabbed hold of the blade again, twisting it to open up the wound even more.
She screamed. A bloodcurdling scream for help. Pitiful. Didn't she know we where miles from the nearest form of civilization? Didn't she know that there was no way anyone was going to hear? Apparantly not.
I slipped the knife from it's newly found sheath of flesh and smiled. The woman fell to the ground, freed from the only thing that kept her standing.
Her crimson life seeped from her slowly as I stood over her, watching...waiting.
Everything was ready before we had even gotten there. I had made sure of that. I made my way around the small circle of stones that I had collected from the nearby river, lighting candles, tracing runes into the earth.
I pulled the woman into position. She was crying again. And uttering completely unintelligable words and curses toward me. That brought about a small chuckle from within my throat. She was about to die... and she knew it.
After everything was set into proper motion, I began the chant that would bring me the greatest power I had ever felt. The full moon shone down brightly as I recited the ancient incantation.
I watched the woman carefully, making sure she would not die before the time was right.
Shouting out the last few syllables, I plunged the knife downward into her heart, grinning as the gout of blood that spewed forth splattered across my face.
Nothing to do now but wait.
Seconds later, I witnessed a spectacle of pure, unadultered power. The sky boiled and rolled with ominous clouds and streaks of lightning. Out of the earth in the circle came a blinding crimson light. Black mist swirled forth from the woman's body and combined with the light as it began to center around me.
* * * *
I awoke later that night... or maybe it was the next night, I couldn't tell. My clothes were caked with blood and gore. I looked toward the circle and saw only a husk of the woman I had used. It had worked. I had the strength. I could feel it coursing through my veins.
My hunger was so intense it hurt. It was time to go test my new power...

Darkness crept over the city. The boy was late... too late. He knew he should have been home by now. Now it was past dark. His eyes darted back and forth... seeing demons in every moving shadow.
There. What was that? Nothing. The boy sighed in relief. Still, his muscles were tensed and ready for action in the event of any sign of trouble.
But apparently not tensed and not ready enough...
He glanced toward another suspected lurker. Just in time to see the most horrid pair of eyes he had ever seen. Then there was darkness...
* * *
So, there I was, right? Hanging out in the alley as usual. Watching the people come and go, searching for that certain someone.
Couple of perks here and there... A VERY busty brunette, a fine, strong young man...
But finally, I saw him.
He couldn't have been older than 9. And he was afraid... very afraid. Perhaps that's what attracted my attention. I have heightened senses, you know?
Anyway, he was looking right and left, that petrified look upon his face. I started toward him... slowly. My lips curled into a smile. My hand clenched at the straight razor in my pocket. I pulled it out and opened the blade.
I think it was the glint of a streetlight reflecting off the blade as I held it against my leg that set the boy off. But it was already too late. His life blood flowed over my hand. My smile grew into a near-snarling grin.
I pulled his body back into the alleyway, the whole time swiping his sweet life across my face. I buried my face in the wound, sucking at and drinking the scalding blood that was spewing forth.
After I had glutted myself, I tossed the boy's body in a nearby dumpster.
It was time to move on to another city. THEY always catch on way too fast...

author: Chaos Creator
content:
Here I sit, trying to record my thoughts, hoping against all hope that my hand can keep up with my mind. My brain whirls so fast sometimes. I don't know why that is. then it all will stop suddenly. I just stop thinking altogether. Like now.
So much to say, Yet, I can't. My pain is constant and sharp. And I wish no better to those around me. In fact, I wish my pain upon others. The infliction of my own wounds upon others. The chaos which I have held within for so long yearns to break free in a primal flow of rage.
And, yet, such I must contain. Never strong enough to say what needs to be said. And the only time I can muster the nerve is always the wrong time.
Bad timing... The story of my life. Heh. Seems as though I might have said that before. But not over 500 times.
Time, time, time.
The only thing we have, and the only thing we never have enough of. We rush and rush all our lives. And for what? Possessions? Titles? The "American Dream"?
And what is the American Dream? Growing old in an assisted care center, waiting for the day we die while wishing all the things we've done in the past could be redeemed?
Or is it merely in our nature to use up and destroy all we come into contact with? Are we simply a race of parasites whose desire for knowledge and power drives us to deplete our resources? Is it this inherant impulse that damns us to a never-ending cycle of creation and destruction?
And if so, Can I hold my father and his father, neither of whome I've ever met, responsible for my actions and the actions of my children? Hardly. We are what we are. I will not apologize for what I am. All I can do is strive to do the best that I can in the situation in which I am placed.
And still, it is and endless pattern. History is constantly repeating itself. And we are constantly depleting ourselves. Depleting ourselves while the world becomes over-populated? Absolutely. Every religious sect, except a few, hold life and nature in high regard. And yet, we are constantly waging wars, killing our fellow man, and raping the earth.
When will we comprehend the fact that we are, in essence, killing ourselves? And, again, for what? Self-preservation? Conceit? Megalomania?
Utopia is impossible. We've preved this fact already. But, perhaps, if we practised a bit more common courtesy toward our fellow earth-dwellers, then maybe there would be something to look forward to.
What kind of home will our children inherit? One countless times more polluted than ours was when handed down, I dare say.
Advancement. Achievement. Technology. Sounds like human folly to me. And yet, we are so dependant upon the technology that is destroying us, and we don't even realize it. Modern medicine is amazing. We can now trouble-shoot the mind almost as well as a computer technician might a PC. Which is great.
But seriously, who needs more advanced weapon systems? We already have the power to destroy whole continents with a single push of a button. Who could ask for more?
Apparantly, our leaders can. Which is why I believe we are all doomed. For, if we cannot choos leaders that can make the right choices, what hope do we have? One voice may not make a difference, but many voices can. And so we vote. And vote. And vote. And what becomes of it? A president with misguided ambitions.
Hey. You wanna reduce drug related crimes? Try something a little different. Instead of forcing people to more daring things (i.e., robbery, theft, murder), try releasing some of the restrictions placed upon drugs.
Take a look at Amsterdam. Drugs are legal there. So is prostitution. Both of which are taxed and somewhat controlled by the government. And the crime raate for drug-related incidents? Almost nil.
I just don't understand. Why spend hundreds of thousands of dollars to combat something you can never fully put an end to, when you could be not only making more money off of it, bust spending those hundreds of thousands on fields in which it is needed.
Which brings me to another question: why does our government see the need to support other countries, when there are people here within our borders who are starving and freezing to deaht because of poverty. Perhaps we should look within, and help ourselves, before reaching out to others. And I mean that litterally and metaphorically.
But I am merely a ranting and raving , "druggie" teenager. What do I know?

I watch the moon trace it never-ending path across the sky as I stand here and smoke my second to last cigarette, thinking about how much my timeless celestial friend and I are alike.
We watch friends and enemies come and go. We've seen countless alliances grow, then dissolve like a grain of salt in the ocean.
Never seen.
Never appreciated.
Our presence seems meaningless at times. And yet, if one of us simply blinked out of existance one day, things would be... different. Changed somehow.
And this I take comfort in. Knowing that if I was not here tomorrow, that someone, somewhere would miss me. I did not believe that not so long ago. I didn't think anyone would care. Many times I've contemplated, and, a couple of times, actually tried, ending my life.
But now I know that people do care. Everyone we meet empowers us. Even the loneliest people have some sembalance (sp?) of friendship. And we should take heart in knowing that if we did vanish, at least one person in the long line of individuals we have interacted with over the years, would look back and say, "Hey... Remember that guy/gal? He/She was really cool. I miss him/her."
And so I say live each day to its fullest. Try and realize your dreams and goals instead of focusing on your failures. Be the best that you can be in whatever strikes your fancy. And remember that, somewhere in this cruel, pretentious world, someone loves you. Even if it is just a heavenly body.
And, to the moon, thanks for being there, and thanks for being and inspiration. I appreciate you even if no one else does.

content:
It was three weeks before the fair started, but you could almost reach out and grab a handful of the excitement that was in the air. There was just something about this place. The mood was one of fun, friendship, and kindred-spirits.
The mock 16-th century village was built to make money and amuse the patrons. But the participants who put on the show enjoyed it just as much or more than the customers. Behind the stages, hidden from view from within the walls of the open air village, acres upon acres of congregations of little dome tents had sprung up. Fair was near at hand.
John and Joseph worked for one of the companies that ran the festival. They had come to assure their returning jobs. They simply enjoyed the freedom that the place offered. And the people were cool, too.
The two arrived Friday evening just to make sure they didn't miss the 8:30 AM meeting on the following morning. They had brought everything they needed for an overnight stay: a tent, blankets, pillows, a change of clothes, a bag of weed, and two hits of really good acid.
So, they set up camp and went around to the groups that had already formed to introduce themselves. They sat and chit-chatted for a while, then retired to their camp for a little... break. John plopped down on the floor of the tent, and Joseph placed himself on the mattress and commenced rolling a joint. Meanwhile, John went to work looking for the little tin that the blotter was in.
Having found it, he popped open the lid and uttered a dismayed gasp. Joseph knew instantly what was wrong. The acid had gone missing. John lit his lighter (for they had no flashlight or lantern) to see if they had fallen in his lap when the tin was opened. But they weren't. Now Joseph was getting anxious. They looked all around the floor of the tent in the meager dual-lighter illumination, but it was no use: the acid was no where to be found.
About that time, an old friend of John's came over to see them. And what did her boyfriend happen to have but a flashlight. The two borrowed the flashlight and went once again on the search, having paused only briefly to say hi and introduce themselves. Joseph took the flashlight and began to sweep the area of the tent, hoping to catch a glimpse of the tiny paper squares. John thought about it for a second, then turned his pockets inside out. And there they went, floating gracefully down into the light cast by the flashlight.
Joseph spied one hit and John saw the other as they hit the ground. Almost instantaneously, the paper pieces no longer lay on the floor of the tent; they were in their respective owners' mouths. Then everything was okay again. Joseph went back to rolling his joint, and John turned his attention to his old friend, Gia.
The quartet stood there talking for a few minutes, almost an hour, actually, while John and Joseph smoked their joint. A short while later, the feeling of giddiness began to creep over them. They began to feel hyperactive, and their minds began to pick up speed. Pretty soon, things started warping out of proportion and the confusion set in.

author: Chaos Creator
content:
The pair of trippers wandered off away from their camp to watch a group of dancers practicing in the street. The actors' bodies went round and round, keeping time with the period music played from a small portable stereo. The weaved back and forth to the melodies of the lute, lyre, and drums, occasionally calling out to one another. It was a strange sight, indeed. John and Joseph sat against an old white Cadellac and watched for half an hour. Then, they wandered on.
Soon, they came to an open field, lit somewhat eerily by sodium-vapor lights. The pair sat down and looked up at the sky, watching the stars twinkle and fade, change locations, and streak across the sky. Joseph lit a cigarette and their conversation took a mor philosophical turn.
They discussed life and death, friends, relationships, anything that happened to cross their drug-altered minds. They sat for hours upon hours in that field, just sharing ideas and opinions, they're out looks on life. Much wisdom was passed between them. And slowly, their words began to form into hallucinations which they could both see.
Down the field a ways, there was a tree backlit by a street light. But, then, it was no longer a tree. It was a young, strong warrior giving a great speech to his clan members. The next instant, the illusion shifted to show an old, bearded man dressed in gray robes sharing his wisdom with the tribe. Finally, the trees morphed into a group of people dancing around a fire.
All of this the two sat and watched, continuing their discussions of the world, pausing here and there to comment on what the tree-people were doing at that moment. For hour after hour they watched the trees and contemplated. They didn't know what time it was, and, in truth, they didn't care. Nothing mattered to the two friends then. Just the truth in the words they were saying.
John and Joseph shared a lifetime of knowledge that night. And something strange happened as they arose to head back to their camp. Joseph lit up another cigarette and looked around at the tree-people. They were all gone. Slightly disturbed, he glanced down the length of the field. And what he saw made him gasp.
There, at the opposite end of the meadow, stood a tall, lithe figure, clad wholly in black robes. Surrounding him, illuminated and givena faint orange hue by the sodium-vapor light, billowed a thick white fog. As he watched, the cloud became thicker and expanded rapidly.
Joseph blinked. When his eyes opened again, the black shape was gone, but the fog remained.
"What is it?" John asked
"I don't know, man. That just fucked me all up..." Joseph replied.
"What?" John asked again.
"There was this dark figure standing over there, and when I blinked it was gone. But the fog it made is still there. See? Look how it's coming up over us. Half the sky you can't even see anymore."
"Who. That is fucked up, dude..."
The two stood there and watched the fog roll slowly toward them, and Joseph said to John, "Maybe we should go back to camp. I feel weird, man."
But John didn't answer.
Joseph turned to ask him again, and then he saw why he didn't answer: he wasn't there. But the fact didn't have time to sink in, because, in the next instant, Joseph blinked out of existance, as well.
John and Joseph had shared a lifetim of knowledge that night...
Fin

author: Chaos Creator
content:
I stare at the t.v. for another hour.
Mindless drivel, all of it.
Blood trickles down my face.
It covers my hands.
I look at the congealing, sticky liquid.
What happened?
I touch my face... my forehead and scalp.
No pain... except for the ringing in my head.
I look in the mirror.
My clothes are torn...
I'm soaked in blood.
Why?
I look back to the t.v.
Same shit.
Always the same shit.
I look around the room.
Nothing out of place.
What's wrong with this picture?
My cigarette burns in the ashtray.
The smoke curls upward until it hits the smog hanging above.
The cigarette is accompanied by several other butts.
How long have I been here?
I walk toward the kitchen...
Past the couch...
Past the cabinet cluttered with all her shit.
Why did she have to have only her stuff everywhere?
Into the kitchen doorway.
I almost slip and fall.
What the fuck?
I look down.
More blood... only it's all in one big pool.
A horrible image flashes in my mind.
A knife... blood splattering...
Things begin to come into focus.
I take another step and looked over.
She lay there on the floor.
Her eyes stared blankly at the ceiling as blood drained from her body.
I gagged.
What had I done?
The knife still protruded from the ripped flesh of her throat.
I fall to the floor.
GOD! Why?
There was a slight sucking/tearing sound as I pulled the knife free.
This can't be! Why? What happened?!
I clutch the knife to my chest as I rock back and forth.
No. Nonononononono...
I stare at the knife.
So much blood.
So much blood...
I bring the knife to my throat.
I pull.
I can feel the burn as the blade eats into my skin.
I feel the warmth as my blood spews forth over my hand.
I watch it as it mingles on the floor with her blood.
My eyelids sag.
My arms feel heavy.
I fall over... half on top of, half beside her.
I close my eyes.
Nononono..n...o...no............ ... ......  .....   ... .... ..   .   .        .
I die.
